metadata.title: Diagnosis and Management of Ectopic Pregnancy
metadata.organization: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) and Association of Early Pregnancy Units (AEPU)
metadata.summary: This guideline provides evidence-based guidance on diagnosing and managing tubal and nontubal ectopic pregnancies. It addresses diagnostic investigations, treatment options, subsequent fertility, patient support, and service and training requirements. Pregnancy of unknown location (PUL) is outside its scope.

target_population: women with suspected or diagnosed ectopic pregnancy

toxicities.incidence: Studies reported rates of 3.9–11.0% after salpingotomy. In an RCT, persistent trophoblast occurred in 14 [7%] women after salpingotomy versus 1 [less than 1%] after salpingectomy (relative risk [RR] 15.0, 95% CI 2.0–113.4).
recognition: Serum b-hCG does not decline as expected after initial treatment.

management.actions: Monitor with serial serum b-hCG measurements and administer methotrexate if levels plateau or rise. Explain that further treatment with systemic methotrexate or salpingectomy may be needed.

toxicities.incidence: One study of interstitial pregnancy reported adverse effects in 40% of women receiving systemic methotrexate; a separate observational study of 17 women treated with systemic methotrexate 50 mg/m2 reported no complications.
recognition: The adverse effects described include marrow suppression, pulmonary fibrosis, nonspecific pneumonitis, liver cirrhosis, renal failure and gastric ulceration.
The most commonly described effects are excessive flatulence and bloating from intestinal gas, a temporary mild increase in liver enzymes and stomatitis.
prevention: Advise women receiving methotrexate to avoid alcohol and folate-containing vitamins during treatment.

toxicities.event: Haemorrhage associated with treatment of cervical pregnancy

management.actions: Reserve surgical management for women with life-threatening bleeding. Uterine artery ligation and uterine artery embolisation (UAE) are described as adjuncts to control haemorrhage.

prevention: Restrict dilatation and curettage to women for whom alternative measures are unsuitable because of its associated risk of excessive bleeding.

toxicities.event: Haemorrhage associated with caesarean scar pregnancy
toxicities.incidence: Among 35 ongoing caesarean section scar pregnancies diagnosed in the first trimester that women chose to continue, 22 ended in emergency hysterectomy at gestational ages of 15 to 38 weeks because of haemorrhage and morbidly adherent placentas.
recognition: Bleeding may occur as retained, highly vascular placental tissue degenerates after medical treatment.
Intra-abdominal rupture and severe vaginal bleeding have been reported at diagnosis or after intervention.

management.actions: Arrange care for morbidly adherent placenta, including a plan for emergency intervention if haemorrhage or rupture occurs. Balance the risks of intervention against those of continuing the pregnancy.

prevention: Some authors have advocated suction evacuation in addition to methotrexate to hasten resolution and reduce unpredictable bleeding during follow-up.

toxicities.event: Haemorrhage associated with placental removal in advanced abdominal pregnancy
recognition: Placental implantation may involve major blood vessels or other vital structures.

management.severity: Placental vascular attachment involving major vessels or vital structures
management.actions: The placenta may be left in situ while spontaneous resorption is awaited. The guideline notes that retention carries significant morbidity, although mortality is lower than with removal.

prevention: Use ultrasound and/or MRI to map the placenta before laparotomy and plan the surgical approach to avoid cutting into it.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Offer anti-D prophylaxis in accordance with national protocol.
prophylaxis.target_population: All RhD-negative women whose ectopic pregnancy is removed surgically, or whose bleeding is repeated, heavy or accompanied by abdominal pain.

therapies_index.name: methotrexate
approved_indications: May be offered systemically to suitable women with tubal ectopic pregnancy; it must not be given at the first visit unless the ectopic diagnosis is certain and a viable intrauterine pregnancy has been excluded.
May be considered for cervical pregnancy.
May be administered locally or systemically for caesarean scar pregnancy or interstitial pregnancy; the guideline does not establish a preferred route for interstitial pregnancy.
May be used systemically for ovarian pregnancy when surgery poses a high risk, or after surgery for persistent residual trophoblast or persistently elevated b-hCG.
Is described as a possible treatment, with ultrasound-guided fetocide, for abdominal pregnancy and as an adjunct to abdominal pregnancy surgery.
For heterotopic pregnancy, should only be considered if the intrauterine pregnancy is nonviable or the woman does not wish to continue the pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: For tubal pregnancy, the usual approach described is a single intramuscular dose of 50 mg/m2, although a multiple-dose regimen is possible. A 50 mg/m2 dose is also described after salpingotomy for persistent trophoblast. For interstitial pregnancy, the guideline describes systemic 50 mg/m2 treatment, a single intravenous dose with oral folinic acid rescue, and intrasaccular injection of 25 mg after aspiration of exocoelomic fluid. Local ultrasound-guided injection into the gestational sac and systemic intramuscular injection are described for caesarean scar pregnancy.
key_toxicities: Excessive flatulence and bloating from intestinal gas
Transient mild elevation of liver enzymes
For caesarean scar pregnancy, retained trophoblast after medical treatment carries a risk of haemorrhage as vascular placental tissue degenerates
In an interstitial pregnancy study, adverse effects were reported in 40% of women receiving systemic methotrexate; the effects were not specified
monitoring: Under the single-dose intramuscular protocol, obtain serum b-hCG, U&E, LFTs, FBC and blood group on day 1, then serum b-hCG on days 4 and 7.
If b-hCG falls by more than 15% between days 4 and 7, measure it weekly until it is less than 15 iu/l.

If b-hCG does not fall by 15% between days 4 and 7, consider repeat transvaginal ultrasound to exclude ectopic fetal cardiac activity and significant haemoperitoneum, followed by consideration of another dose if criteria for medical management remain satisfied.
Women receiving methotrexate should be able and willing to attend follow-up.

therapies_index.name: potassium chloride
approved_indications: Local injection is described for cervical pregnancy.
Intrasaccular injection with methotrexate is described for interstitial pregnancy.
Injection before later rudimentary horn excision is reported for cornual pregnancy.
Local injection with aspiration of sac contents is an option for clinically stable women with heterotopic pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: For interstitial pregnancy, the described intrasaccular dose is 0.2–0.4 mEq, with or without methotrexate. For heterotopic pregnancy, injection is into the fetal pole if possible, or otherwise into the extrauterine sac, together with aspiration of sac contents.
monitoring: Following local treatment of heterotopic pregnancy, ultrasound follow-up is necessary to confirm resolution because b-hCG cannot be used for that purpose.

therapies_index.name: hyperosmolar glucose
approved_indications: Local injection with aspiration of sac contents is an option for clinically stable women with heterotopic pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Injected into the extrauterine sac alongside aspiration of its contents.
monitoring: Ultrasound follow-up is necessary to establish resolution of the ectopic component; b-hCG cannot be used.

therapies_index.name: folinic acid
approved_indications: Oral rescue treatment accompanying a single intravenous dose of methotrexate was described in a case series of interstitial pregnancies.
therapies_index.administration: Given orally as part of the reported intravenous methotrexate and oral folinic acid rescue regimen; no dose is specified.

therapies_index.name: vasopressin
approved_indications: A diluted preparation was described for haemostasis during laparoscopic surgery for interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: In the reported technique, 1 ampoule [20 U] was diluted in 1000 ml of normal saline [1000-fold], and 150–250 ml [0.02 U/ml] was injected into the uterus beneath the interstitial pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: etoposide
therapies_index.mechanism: The guideline identifies it as a topoisomerase II inhibitor.
approved_indications: Successful intra-amniotic use was reported in a case of 12-week interstitial pregnancy after systemic methotrexate had failed; the guideline does not recommend it as a routine treatment.
therapies_index.administration: Intra-amniotic injection was reported; no dose is given.

therapies_index.name: anti-D immunoglobulin
approved_indications: Anti-D prophylaxis should be offered according to national protocol to RhD-negative women after surgical removal of an ectopic pregnancy, or when bleeding is recurrent, heavy or accompanied by abdominal pain.
therapies_index.administration: According to national protocol; the guideline gives no dose or route.

therapies_index.name: single-dose intravenous methotrexate and oral folinic acid rescue regimen
approved_indications: A case series reported this regimen for interstitial pregnancy; it is presented as a reported approach rather than a preferred regimen.
therapies_index.administration: A single intravenous methotrexate dose with oral folinic acid rescue; component doses are not specified.

therapies_index.name: expectant management
approved_indications: An option for clinically stable women with an ultrasound diagnosis of tubal ectopic pregnancy and decreasing b-hCG initially less than 1500 iu/l.
Only suitable for interstitial pregnancy when b-hCG is low or falling significantly and adding methotrexate may not improve the outcome.

May be suitable for a small, nonviable caesarean scar pregnancy; it may also be considered under the stated counselling and patient-choice conditions when a pregnancy is partially implanted in the scar and grows into the uterine cavity.
An option for heterotopic pregnancy when ultrasound findings indicate that the ectopic pregnancy is nonviable.
therapies_index.administration: For tubal pregnancy, selection and counselling include clinical stability, minimal pain and willingness and ability to return for follow-up. In a reported observational protocol, repeat b-hCG testing was individualised at intervals of 2 to 7 days; expectant management stopped for patient choice, significant pain, a sustained b-hCG rise or a rise to greater than 2000 iu/l.
key_toxicities: Continuing a caesarean scar pregnancy can involve haemorrhage and morbidly adherent placentation.
monitoring: For tubal pregnancy, follow serum b-hCG; the reported observational protocol continued until it was less than 20 iu/l.
For caesarean scar pregnancy that continues, counselling about haemorrhage and morbidly adherent placentation is required.
For heterotopic pregnancy, assessment cannot rely on b-hCG to establish resolution of the ectopic component.

therapies_index.name: laparoscopy
approved_indications: The preferred surgical approach over an open approach for tubal pregnancy.
An approach for excision of the rudimentary horn in cornual pregnancy.
An option for removing early abdominal pregnancy when the implantation site does not involve a vascular area.
A minimally invasive approach used to treat ovarian pregnancy and an option for removal of an accessible ectopic component of heterotopic pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Requires suitable equipment and trained theatre staff. During surgery for heterotopic pregnancy, uterine cannulation or manipulation should be avoided.

therapies_index.name: laparotomy
approved_indications: An approach for excision of the rudimentary horn in cornual pregnancy.
Advanced abdominal pregnancy should be managed by laparotomy.
therapies_index.administration: For advanced abdominal pregnancy, the operative plan should avoid cutting through the placenta.

therapies_index.name: salpingectomy
approved_indications: Should be performed rather than salpingotomy for tubal pregnancy when the opposite tube is healthy.
May be needed after salpingotomy if further treatment becomes necessary.
therapies_index.administration: A laparoscopic approach is preferred to an open approach for tubal surgery.

therapies_index.name: salpingotomy
approved_indications: Should be considered for tubal pregnancy in women with fertility-reducing factors.
Laparoscopic salpingotomy is an effective surgical option for interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: May be performed laparoscopically. Women should be counselled before tubal salpingotomy about persistent trophoblast and the possibility of further treatment with systemic methotrexate or salpingectomy.
key_toxicities: A small risk of needing additional treatment after tubal salpingotomy
monitoring: Serial serum b-hCG measurements are needed after tubal salpingotomy to detect persistent trophoblast.
The cited NICE guidance specifies serum b-hCG at 7 days after surgery and weekly thereafter until a negative result.

therapies_index.name: laparoscopic cornual resection
approved_indications: An effective surgical option for interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Performed laparoscopically; the guideline does not specify a standard operative technique.

therapies_index.name: hysteroscopic resection
approved_indications: A possible alternative for interstitial pregnancy under laparoscopic or ultrasound guidance.
A described method of evacuating caesarean scar pregnancy.
Reported in combination with UAE for cervical pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: For interstitial pregnancy, laparoscopic visualisation or ultrasound guidance may be used. A small cervical pregnancy case series combined the procedure with UAE.

therapies_index.name: dilatation and curettage
approved_indications: A historically used cervical pregnancy treatment whose use should be restricted to women for whom alternative measures are unsuitable.
therapies_index.administration: Additional measures to limit haemorrhage have traditionally accompanied the procedure.
key_toxicities: High rates of excessive bleeding requiring hysterectomy were reported in cervical pregnancy

therapies_index.name: uterine artery ligation
approved_indications: Described as an adjunct to control haemorrhage during cervical pregnancy treatment.

therapies_index.name: uterine artery embolisation (UAE)
approved_indications: Described as an adjunct for haemorrhage control in cervical pregnancy, including with hysteroscopic resection or methotrexate.
Described as an additional haemostatic measure with suction evacuation of caesarean scar pregnancy.
Selective UAE with methotrexate is reported for interstitial pregnancy to reduce haemorrhage.
therapies_index.administration: Performed as an embolisation procedure; the guideline does not specify a technique.
key_toxicities: Complications reported for cervical pregnancy haemorrhage-control methods used with methotrexate include infection, uterine infarction, sciatic nerve injury, and necrosis of the bladder or rectum; the guideline does not assign each event to a specific method.
For selective UAE in interstitial pregnancy, safety and complications in future pregnancies are uncertain

therapies_index.name: suction evacuation
approved_indications: A described surgical method for evacuating caesarean scar pregnancy, sometimes added to methotrexate to hasten resolution and reduce unpredictable follow-up haemorrhage.
therapies_index.administration: Has been combined with cervical cerclage, Foley catheter insertion or UAE as additional haemostatic measures.

therapies_index.name: cervical cerclage
approved_indications: Described as an additional haemostatic measure with suction evacuation of caesarean scar pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Used in combination with suction evacuation; no further technique is specified.

therapies_index.name: Foley catheter insertion
approved_indications: Described as an additional haemostatic measure with suction evacuation of caesarean scar pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Used in combination with suction evacuation; no further technique is specified.

therapies_index.name: excision of the pregnancy
approved_indications: A described surgical approach for caesarean scar pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Open, laparoscopic and transvaginal procedures are described. Excisional techniques can incorporate scar repair, but whether repair reduces recurrence or future scar rupture is unknown.
key_toxicities: The described excisional procedures are more invasive and technically more difficult than evacuation

therapies_index.name: excision of the rudimentary horn
approved_indications: Cornual pregnancy should be managed by this procedure to avoid recurrence.
therapies_index.administration: May be performed by laparoscopy or laparotomy. The described laparoscopic technique divides the fibrous attachment to the unicornuate uterus and removes the horn through a secondary port.
monitoring: Attention should be paid to possible associated urinary tract anomalies.

therapies_index.name: enucleation
approved_indications: A preferred method for removing gestational products in ovarian pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Blunt removal from the ovary is described as minimising damage to adjacent ovarian tissue.

therapies_index.name: wedge resection
approved_indications: A preferred method for removing gestational products when an ovarian ectopic mass is large.
therapies_index.administration: Performed as ovarian surgery; no further technique is specified.

therapies_index.name: oophorectomy
approved_indications: Occasionally required for ovarian pregnancy when ipsilateral ovarian pathology coexists or bleeding is excessive.

therapies_index.name: electrocautery
approved_indications: A described means of achieving haemostasis during ovarian pregnancy surgery.
therapies_index.administration: Applied for haemostasis after removal of ovarian gestational products.

therapies_index.name: suturing
approved_indications: A described means of achieving haemostasis during ovarian pregnancy surgery.
therapies_index.administration: Used for haemostasis after removal of ovarian gestational products.

therapies_index.name: ultrasoundguided fetocide
approved_indications: Described as a possible alternative treatment for abdominal pregnancy when combined with systemic methotrexate.
therapies_index.administration: Ultrasound-guided; no further method is specified.

therapies_index.name: aspiration of the sac contents
approved_indications: An option with local potassium chloride or hyperosmolar glucose injection for clinically stable women with heterotopic pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Performed alongside injection into the extrauterine pregnancy.
monitoring: Ultrasound follow-up is necessary to confirm resolution of the ectopic pregnancy because b-hCG cannot be used.

therapies_index.name: transvaginal ultrasoundguided aspiration of the exocoelomic fluid
approved_indications: A reported step before intrasaccular methotrexate injection for interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Exocoelomic fluid is aspirated from the gestational sac under transvaginal ultrasound guidance before intrasaccular injection.

therapies_index.name: electrocauterisation
approved_indications: A reported endoscopic approach for interstitial pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: endoloop application
approved_indications: A reported endoscopic approach before evacuation of an interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Applied before evacuation of the conceptus.

therapies_index.name: encircling suture
approved_indications: A reported endoscopic approach before evacuation of an interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Placed before evacuation of the conceptus.

therapies_index.name: laparoscopic haemostatic suturing techniques
approved_indications: Reported for surgical treatment of interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Performed laparoscopically; no single technique is specified.

therapies_index.name: ‘purse-string’ technique
approved_indications: Reported for laparoscopic resection of interstitial pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Used during laparoscopic resection; no further procedural details are given.

therapies_index.name: ultrasound-guided dilatation and evacuation using polypectomy forceps
approved_indications: Reported in a small case series for interstitial pregnancy, followed by single-dose systemic methotrexate.
therapies_index.administration: Performed under ultrasound guidance with polypectomy forceps, then followed by single-dose systemic methotrexate.

therapies_index.name: selective arterial embolisation
approved_indications: Described as an adjunctive treatment for advanced abdominal pregnancy.

therapies_index.name: preoperative angiographic embolisation
approved_indications: A potential perioperative measure when imaging identifies placental implantation near vital structures in abdominal pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: Considered before surgery; no technique is specified.

therapies_index.name: muscle relaxation training
approved_indications: May help women receiving methotrexate for ectopic pregnancy.
therapies_index.administration: An RCT used adjuvant training based on the Bernstein and Borkovec technique; the guideline gives no schedule.

conditions.name: ectopic pregnancy
conditions.description: A pregnancy implanted outside the endometrial cavity. The guideline addresses tubal, cervical, caesarean scar, interstitial, cornual, ovarian, abdominal and heterotopic pregnancies; it does not address pregnancy of unknown location.
conditions.epidemiology: In the UK, incidence is approximately 11/1000 pregnancies, with an estimated 11 000 diagnoses each year. Among women attending early pregnancy units, incidence is 2–3%. Six maternal deaths were reported between 2006 and 2008. Risk factors include tubal injury after surgery or infection, smoking and in vitro fertilisation, although the majority of affected women have no identifiable risk factor.

subtypes.name: caesarean scar pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Implantation in a myometrial defect at a previous uterine incision.

subtypes.name: interstitial pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Implantation in the interstitial portion of a fallopian tube.

subtypes.name: cornual pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The guideline distinguishes implantation associated with an abnormally formed uterine horn from interstitial pregnancy, while noting that some authors use the terms interchangeably.

subtypes.name: ovarian pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The suspected gestation is associated with the ovary.

subtypes.name: abdominal pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The gestation is situated in the abdomen rather than the uterine cavity.

subtypes.name: heterotopic pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: An intrauterine pregnancy coexists with an ectopic pregnancy.

long_term_effects: Studies cited by the guideline found no statistically significant difference in recurrent ectopic pregnancy rates between management methods; most long-term follow-up studies report a rate of around 18.5%.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline advises making treatment and follow-up information available in writing and recording the follow-up plan in the early pregnancy clinic discharge letter. It also notes that pregnancy loss may have substantial psychological effects on women, partners and families, and that women may need support during subsequent pregnancies.

conditions.name: tubal pregnancy
conditions.description: An ectopic gestation in a fallopian tube. Where possible, ultrasound identification relies on an adnexal mass that moves independently of the ovary.
conditions.clinical_presentation: An adnexal mass is the usual sonographic finding. Echogenic pelvic fluid can indicate rupture, although it more often reflects bleeding from the fimbrial end of the tube. Neither free fluid alone nor an intrauterine fluid collection alone establishes the diagnosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Preferred diagnostic examination for tubal ectopic pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When tubal ectopic pregnancy is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Where possible, identify an adnexal mass moving separately from the ovary. Reported sensitivity for ectopic pregnancy is 87.0–99.0% and specificity is 94.0–99.9%. An inhomogeneous or noncystic adnexal mass occurs in around 50–60% of cases, an empty extrauterine gestational sac in around 20–40%, and an extrauterine sac containing a yolk sac and/or embryonic pole, with or without cardiac activity, in around 15–20%. An ectopic pregnancy may be too early or small to appear on the initial examination.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment of the uterine cavity and pelvic fluid on ultrasound
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Distinguish findings that support an intrauterine gestation from nonspecific findings.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During sonographic assessment of suspected tubal pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: No particular endometrial appearance or thickness establishes tubal pregnancy. Intrauterine fluid, sometimes termed a ‘pseudosac’, occurs in up to 20% of cases but cannot alone establish ectopic pregnancy. In a cited study, women with a positive pregnancy test, a smooth-walled intrauterine anechoic cystic structure and no adnexal mass had a 0.02% probability of ectopic pregnancy and a 99.98% probability of intrauterine pregnancy. A small amount of anechoic fluid in the pouch of Douglas can accompany either intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy. Echogenic fluid was reported in 28–56% of ectopic pregnancies and may indicate rupture.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assessment of its value for predicting ectopic pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The level is not useful for predicting ectopic pregnancy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform management and the likely success of conservative treatment after ultrasound visualisation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When planning management of an ultrasound-visualised ectopic pregnancy; repeat testing can help clarify management when the diagnosis is uncertain.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A single value cannot independently predict ectopic pregnancy, and a value less than 1000 iu/l does not make it unlikely. The initial value helps predict outcomes of expectant and medical management. Before methotrexate in cases appearing as an inhomogeneous mass, the guideline considers repeating the measurement in 48 hours prudent: a fall may support expectant management, whereas a rise compatible with viable intrauterine pregnancy calls for reassessment of the diagnosis by ultrasound.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Surgical assessment rather than the diagnostic reference standard.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: It is no longer considered the diagnostic gold standard. False-negative results of 3.0–4.5% have been reported when performed too early in a continuing ectopic pregnancy.

follow_up.schedule: After salpingotomy, the cited NICE guidance calls for serum b-hCG at 7 days after surgery and weekly thereafter until the result is negative. Following single-dose methotrexate, measure serum b-hCG on days 4 and 7; if it falls by more than 15% between days 4 and 7, continue weekly measurements until less than 15 iu/l. In a cited observational expectant-management protocol, repeat b-hCG intervals varied between 2 and 7 days and follow-up continued until less than 20 iu/l.
recommended_tests: Serial serum b-hCG after salpingotomy to identify persistent trophoblast.
Serum b-hCG on days 4 and 7 and, when the specified decline occurs, weekly after methotrexate.
Consider repeat transvaginal ultrasound if serum b-hCG does not decrease by 15% between days 4 and 7 after methotrexate, to assess ectopic fetal cardiac activity and significant haemoperitoneum.
long_term_effects: Persistent trophoblast may occur after salpingotomy and may require systemic methotrexate or salpingectomy.
In women without previous subfertility or tubal pathology, the guideline reports no difference between management methods in fertility, future tubal ectopic pregnancy risk or tubal patency.
For women with previous subfertility, expectant or medical treatment is associated with better reproductive outcomes than radical surgery.

The guideline states that methotrexate treatment does not affect ovarian reserve. It also cites limited evidence of lower oocyte yield when fertility treatment resumes within 180 days of methotrexate.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Women treated with methotrexate are advised to wait at least 3 months before attempting conception. The guideline states that conception within 3 months of treatment is not, by itself, an indication for termination.

conditions.name: cervical pregnancy
conditions.description: An ectopic gestation implanted in the cervix; an implanted sac does not slide along the endocervical canal when probe pressure is applied.
conditions.epidemiology: Cervical pregnancies account for less than 1% of ectopic gestations.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Life-threatening bleeding is a consideration in treatment selection.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess features supporting cervical implantation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When cervical ectopic pregnancy is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The described features are an empty uterine cavity, a barrel-shaped cervix, a gestational sac below the internal cervical os, an absent ‘sliding sign’, and blood flow around the sac on colour Doppler.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Distinguish an implanted cervical pregnancy from a miscarriage in the cervical canal.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When a gestational sac is seen in the cervix.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A sac associated with miscarriage moves against the endocervical canal with probe pressure; an implanted cervical sac does not.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess vascularity around the cervical gestational sac.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During ultrasound evaluation for cervical pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Flow surrounding the gestational sac is among the described diagnostic features.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help select management after diagnosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At the time of ultrasound diagnosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A level greater than 10 000 iu/l is associated with a lower likelihood of successful methotrexate treatment.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: A cited retrospective review associated gestational age more than 9+0 weeks, b-hCG greater than 10 000 iu/l, crown–rump length greater than 10 mm and fetal cardiac activity with greater risk of primary failure of systemic methotrexate. The guideline also associates gestational age less than 12+0 weeks, absent fetal cardiac activity and lower serum b-hCG with more successful conservative management.

conditions.name: caesarean scar pregnancy
conditions.description: Implantation into a myometrial defect at a previous uterine incision. A pregnancy at this site may continue with potential viability or miscarry within the scar.
conditions.epidemiology: Estimated prevalence is approximately 1 in 2000 pregnancies. The guideline notes that this may underestimate the true prevalence because some pregnancies end and remain unrecognised or unreported. Thirteen percent of reported cases were initially mistaken for intrauterine or cervical pregnancy.
conditions.clinical_presentation: The guideline associates these pregnancies with severe maternal morbidity and mortality. Possible courses include major bleeding at the implantation site or progression towards the uterine serosa with first trimester rupture and haemorrhage.

subtypes.name: first type
subtypes.distinguishing_features: In the classification proposed by Vial et al., the growing sac extends towards the uterine cavity and may reach a viable gestational age, but carries a risk of major implantation-site bleeding.

subtypes.name: second
subtypes.distinguishing_features: In the classification proposed by Vial et al., implantation extends more deeply towards the uterine serosa, with a risk of first trimester rupture and haemorrhage.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Primary diagnostic examination.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When implantation in a caesarean scar is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Described findings are an empty uterine cavity; a sac or solid trophoblastic mass anteriorly at the internal os within a previous lower uterine segment scar; thin or absent myometrium between the sac and bladder; conspicuous trophoblastic or placental Doppler circulation; and an empty endocervical canal. These diagnostic criteria have not been validated and come from descriptive case series.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Supplement transvaginal imaging.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: If additional imaging is required.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess trophoblastic or placental circulation at the suspected scar implantation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As part of the sonographic assessment.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Prominent circulation is one of the described diagnostic features.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Clarify an uncertain diagnosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As a second-line examination when the diagnosis is equivocal and local expertise in MRI diagnosis of these pregnancies is available.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The described MRI appearances are essentially similar to those on ultrasound.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide a baseline if monitoring during conservative treatment is planned.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When conservative treatment is being considered; biochemical testing is not routinely needed for diagnosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Serum b-hCG has no diagnostic role for caesarean scar pregnancy.

long_term_effects: The guideline states that it is unknown whether repairing the scar during excisional treatment lowers the risk of recurrent caesarean scar pregnancy or scar rupture in a subsequent pregnancy.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Because the diagnostic criteria are unvalidated, the guideline recommends regional-centre confirmation for suspected cases that are not emergencies. For ongoing second trimester scar pregnancy, it calls for a care plan addressing morbidly adherent placenta and emergency intervention if haemorrhage or rupture occurs.

conditions.name: interstitial pregnancy
conditions.description: An ectopic pregnancy implanted in the interstitial segment of a fallopian tube. This segment measures about 1–2 cm, passes through the uterine wall's muscular myometrium and opens into the uterine cavity.
conditions.epidemiology: Reported incidence ranges from 1.0% to 6.3% of ectopic pregnancies.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify interstitial implantation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When interstitial pregnancy is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Described criteria include an empty uterine cavity, a laterally placed gestational sac or products of conception in the interstitial (intramural) tube with less than 5 mm of surrounding myometrium in every imaging plane, and the ‘interstitial line sign’. The reported sensitivity of that sign is 80% and its specificity is 98%.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Further assess two-dimensional findings and avoid confusion with early intrauterine or angular pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Where available.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A coronal uterine view may show the connection between the endometrial cavity and the interstitial tube.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Supplement diagnosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When additional imaging is helpful.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Described supportive findings include a sac-like structure lateral to the cornua within myometrium and an intact junctional zone between that structure and the uterine cavity.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform the choice among management options, rather than establish the diagnosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At presentation when symptoms and ultrasound raise suspicion.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The result contributes to management decisions alongside clinical presentation, pregnancy size and fetal cardiac activity.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help determine further management.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In some cases, particularly a small pregnancy identified by ultrasound.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A repeat measurement in 48 hours may be useful.

long_term_effects: The guideline considers evidence insufficient to recommend other nonsurgical approaches because their safety and effects on future pregnancies are uncertain.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: In a cited case series of 42 women, successful expectant and medical management was associated with lower initial b-hCG than unsuccessful management (3216 iu/l versus 15 900 iu/l; P < 0.05).

conditions.name: cornual pregnancy
conditions.description: The guideline uses cornual pregnancy for a gestation associated with a congenitally abnormal uterine horn, while acknowledging that some authors use ‘cornual’ and ‘interstitial’ interchangeably.
conditions.epidemiology: Under the congenital-horn definition used in the guideline, reported incidence is 1 in 76 000 pregnancies.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the described features of cornual implantation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When cornual pregnancy is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Described findings are one visible interstitial segment of fallopian tube in the main uterine body; a mobile gestational sac or products of conception separate from the uterus and fully enclosed by myometrium; and a vascular pedicle connecting the sac to the unicornuate uterus.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Plan management.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis when symptoms and ultrasound suggest cornual pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Management decisions also depend on clinical presentation and pregnancy size.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assist subsequent management decisions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In some cases with a small cornual pregnancy seen on ultrasound.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A repeat level in 48 hours may be helpful.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline favours removal of the rudimentary horn to avoid recurrence and notes the possibility of associated urinary tract anomalies in women with a unicornuate uterus.

conditions.name: ovarian pregnancy
conditions.description: An ectopic gestation involving an ovary. It can be difficult to distinguish from a corpus luteal cyst, a tubal pregnancy adherent to the ovary, a second corpus luteum, ovarian germ cell tumours or other ovarian disease.
conditions.clinical_presentation: A complex echogenic adnexal mass together with free fluid in the pouch of Douglas may represent rupture.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify findings suggestive of ovarian implantation, although specific agreed diagnostic criteria are unavailable.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When ovarian ectopic pregnancy is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: With an empty uterus, a broad echogenic ring containing an anechoic area on the ovary may be seen; a yolk sac or embryo is less common. The suspected sac or cystic structure cannot be separated from the ovary by gentle palpation, giving a negative sliding organ sign. The corpus luteum should be identified separately.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Look for fetal cardiac pulsation within the ovary.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of a suspected ovarian pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: It may help identify a fetal heartbeat.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help plan management.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assist further management decisions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In some cases.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A repeat measurement in 48 hours may be useful.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish the diagnosis surgically when imaging cannot distinguish ovarian pregnancy from other conditions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When surgical diagnosis is required.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The diagnosis is usually confirmed surgically and histologically.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm ovarian ectopic pregnancy after surgical treatment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Following surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The histopathology result confirms the diagnosis.

long_term_effects: The guideline describes future fertility after laparoscopic management as good. In a cited small case series, 100% conceived again and 83% achieved a live birth.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: For methotrexate treatment of ovarian pregnancy, the guideline states that defined selection criteria and treatment or follow-up regimens are unavailable.

conditions.name: abdominal pregnancy
conditions.description: An ectopic pregnancy in the abdomen. The guideline addresses early and advanced presentations separately.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Advanced abdominal pregnancy is associated with substantial maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality. Placental attachment to major vessels or other vital structures can complicate surgical removal.

subtypes.name: early abdominal pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The guideline describes sonographic criteria for an early abdominal gestation and notes that it is usually identified at laparoscopy during investigation of persistently elevated serum b-hCG.

subtypes.name: advanced abdominal pregnancy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: MRI may help establish placental attachment and plan surgery; the guideline calls for prompt laparotomy after diagnosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess for abdominal implantation and, before surgery, locate the placenta.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When abdominal pregnancy is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Published criteria for early pregnancy comprise no intrauterine sac, no evident dilated tube or complex adnexal mass, a gestational cavity surrounded by bowel loops and separated from them by peritoneum, and marked sac mobility resembling fluctuation when the transvaginal probe presses towards the posterior cul-de-sac.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help confirm advanced abdominal pregnancy, identify placental attachment to vital structures and guide surgical planning.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When ultrasound identifies or strongly suggests abdominal pregnancy in a clinically stable patient, particularly in advanced pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Ultrasound and/or MRI can map placental location before laparotomy to help avoid cutting through the placenta.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Contribute to suspicion when considered together with ultrasound findings.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment for abdominal pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An elevated level combined with ultrasound findings raises suspicion; persistent elevation may prompt investigation during which early abdominal pregnancy is diagnosed.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify an early abdominal pregnancy during investigation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As described for investigation of persistently elevated serum b-hCG.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Early abdominal pregnancy is usually diagnosed at laparoscopy in this setting.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: For advanced pregnancy, the guideline notes that leaving the placenta in place when it is attached to major vessels or vital structures can lead to ileus, bowel obstruction, fistula, haemorrhage or peritonitis, although mortality is lower than with placental removal.

conditions.name: heterotopic pregnancy
conditions.description: Coexistence of an intrauterine pregnancy and an ectopic pregnancy.
conditions.clinical_presentation: The guideline calls for consideration of this diagnosis after assisted reproductive technologies, with persistent pelvic pain despite a known intrauterine pregnancy, or with persistently elevated b-hCG following miscarriage or termination.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish the coexistence of intrauterine and ectopic gestations.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When heterotopic pregnancy is suspected, including in the clinical situations described by the guideline.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Diagnosis rests on visualising both an intrauterine pregnancy and a concurrent ectopic pregnancy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess its limited diagnostic contribution.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During evaluation of suspected heterotopic pregnancy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Its diagnostic value is limited. A value higher than expected for gestational age may raise suspicion, but a complete or partial mole must also be considered. In a cited case series of 20 heterotopic pregnancies after assisted reproductive technology, the mean value at pregnancy testing was not higher than in nonheterotopic pregnancies.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm resolution of the ectopic component after local injection and aspiration.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: After this form of medical management.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Serum b-hCG cannot be used to establish resolution in this setting.

recommended_tests: Ultrasound after local treatment of the ectopic component to check that it resolves.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: The prognosis of the intrauterine pregnancy and the woman's wishes about continuing it must inform management. The guideline states that b-hCG cannot be used to monitor resolution of the ectopic component after local injection and aspiration.

special_populations.population: RhD-negative women with an ectopic pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: Alloimmunisation has been reported after ectopic pregnancy. The guideline notes that evidence is limited for the risk associated with medical or expectant management.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Offer anti-D prophylaxis according to national protocol after surgical removal of an ectopic pregnancy, or when bleeding is recurrent, heavy or accompanied by abdominal pain.

special_populations.population: Women with fertility-reducing factors and tubal ectopic pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: The factors identified are previous ectopic pregnancy, damage to the contralateral tube, previous abdominal surgery and previous pelvic inflammatory disease.

special_populations.population: Women with a healthy contralateral tube and tubal ectopic pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: In this group, salpingotomy does not significantly improve subsequent fertility compared with salpingectomy.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Perform salpingectomy in preference to salpingotomy.

special_populations.population: Women with a previous history of subfertility
special_populations.considerations: For tubal ectopic pregnancy, expectant or medical management is associated with better reproductive outcomes than radical surgery. The guideline particularly notes lower subsequent intrauterine pregnancy rates after radical surgery among women with subfertility who are over the age of 35 years.

special_populations.population: Women without a history of subfertility or tubal pathology
special_populations.considerations: Counsel women that the management methods do not differ in fertility rates, future tubal ectopic pregnancy risk or tubal patency rates.

special_populations.population: Women with a heterotopic pregnancy and a viable intrauterine pregnancy, or who wish to continue the intrauterine pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: The prognosis of the intrauterine pregnancy and the woman's wishes must inform management. Serum b-hCG cannot be used to confirm resolution of the ectopic pregnancy after local treatment.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Do not use methotrexate when the intrauterine pregnancy is viable or the woman wishes to continue it. Local injection of potassium chloride or hyperosmolar glucose with aspiration of sac contents is an option for clinically stable women; use ultrasound to monitor resolution.

special_populations.population: Haemodynamically unstable women with heterotopic pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: The coexisting intrauterine pregnancy must remain part of the management plan.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Surgical removal of the ectopic pregnancy is the method of choice.

special_populations.population: Women with an ongoing second trimester caesarean scar pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: Maternal morbidity and hysterectomy risks are high whichever approach is used. The risks of intervention must be weighed against those of continuing the pregnancy toward a potentially viable gestational age.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Arrange care for morbidly adherent placenta and a plan for emergency intervention if haemorrhage or rupture occurs.

special_populations.population: Clinically stable women with suspected caesarean scar pregnancy
special_populations.considerations: The diagnostic criteria have not been validated, and the condition may be difficult to diagnose.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Refer nonemergency suspected cases to a regional centre to confirm the diagnosis. Women who are clinically stable should be managed by a multidisciplinary team with relevant expertise.

special_populations.population: Women planning conception after methotrexate treatment
special_populations.considerations: The guideline reports concern about subsequent pregnancy and fetal development. Conception within 3 months of methotrexate exposure should not, by itself, be considered an indication for termination.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Wait at least 3 months after methotrexate treatment before attempting conception.

special_populations.considerations: Breastfeeding is listed as a contraindication to methotrexate.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Do not use methotrexate while breastfeeding.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women requiring surgery who have a healthy contralateral tube.
decision_rules: Prefer laparoscopy to an open operation.
When the contralateral tube is healthy, perform salpingectomy rather than salpingotomy.

recommended_regimens.name: laparoscopic surgical approach
recommended_regimens.summary: The laparoscopic approach is preferred to laparotomy for surgical treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: salpingectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Remove the affected tube in preference to salpingotomy when the other tube is healthy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a multicentre RCT of 446 women, cumulative ongoing pregnancy occurred in 56.2% after salpingectomy versus 60.7% after salpingotomy; the trial concluded that salpingotomy did not significantly improve fertility. Persistent trophoblast occurred in 1 [less than 1%] after salpingectomy versus 14 [7%] after salpingotomy (RR 15.0, 95% CI 2.0–113.4). Repeat ectopic pregnancy occurred in 12 (5%) after salpingectomy versus 18 (8%) after salpingotomy (RR 1.6, 95% CI 0.8–3.3).

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Compared with laparotomy, laparoscopy is associated with shorter surgery and hospitalisation, less operative blood loss and adhesion formation, and lower costs and analgesic needs. The guideline reports no difference in health benefits, including later successful pregnancy.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with fertility-reducing factors, including previous ectopic pregnancy, contralateral tubal damage, previous abdominal surgery or previous pelvic inflammatory disease.
decision_rules: Consider salpingotomy when fertility-reducing factors are present.
After salpingotomy, explain the possibility of persistent trophoblast, the need for serum b-hCG surveillance and the small possibility of further treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: salpingotomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider tubal-conserving surgery in women with a history of fertility-reducing factors.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: One study reported subsequent intrauterine pregnancy in 75% after salpingotomy versus 40% after salpingectomy among women with fertility-reducing factors. Studies reported persistent trophoblast in 3.9–11.0% after salpingotomy.

response_assessment.timepoint: 7 days after surgery, then weekly until a negative result
response_assessment.interpretation: NICE recommends this schedule after salpingotomy. A level that fails to fall as expected indicates persistent trophoblast; levels that plateau or rise may prompt methotrexate.

supportive_care: Counsel about persistent trophoblast and the possibility of subsequent systemic methotrexate or salpingectomy.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline states that definitive predictors of persistent trophoblast after salpingotomy have not been established.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Suitable women who are haemodynamically stable, can attend follow-up, have no known sensitivity to methotrexate, have no intrauterine pregnancy and have no fetal cardiac activity on ultrasound; a low serum b-hCG is preferred.
decision_rules: Systemic methotrexate may be offered to appropriately selected women.
Do not administer it at the first visit unless ectopic pregnancy is unequivocally diagnosed and a viable intrauterine pregnancy has been excluded.
A favourable candidate has serum b-hCG ideally less than 1500 iu/l, although it can be up to 5000 iu/l.

If the diagnosis remains uncertain, repeat serum b-hCG in 48 hours; a falling value may favour expectant management, whereas a rise compatible with viable intrauterine pregnancy warrants another scan before methotrexate.

NICE recommends methotrexate as first-line management for women able to return for follow-up who have no significant pain, an unruptured mass smaller than 35 mm without a visible heartbeat, serum b-hCG between 1500 and 5000 iu/l, and no intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound.

recommended_regimens.name: systemic methotrexate
recommended_regimens.summary: Medical treatment is an option for suitable women with a confirmed tubal ectopic pregnancy. The commonly used schedule is a single intramuscular dose of 50 mg/m2.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reported success with single-dose methotrexate ranges from 65–95%, and 3–27% of women require a second dose. The largest cited study reported success in 90.7% (507/559). Reported success was 81–98% when serum b-hCG was less than 1000 iu/l, compared with 38% when it was greater than 5000 iu/l. Studies reported success of 88–100% when serum b-hCG fell from day 1 to day 4, versus 42–62% when it rose.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Single intramuscular dose of 50 mg/m2; consider another 50 mg/m2 dose if follow-up criteria are not met and the woman remains eligible.

not_recommended.name: methotrexate at the first visit without a certain diagnosis
not_recommended.reason: A viable intrauterine pregnancy must first be excluded unless the ectopic diagnosis is absolutely clear.

response_assessment.interpretation: If the decline between days 4 and 7 is more than 15%, continue weekly measurements until the level is less than 15 iu/l. If it does not decrease by 15%, consider repeat transvaginal ultrasound to exclude ectopic fetal cardiac activity and significant haemoperitoneum, followed by consideration of another dose.

response_assessment.timepoint: weekly after an adequate decline between days 4 and 7

supportive_care: Advise avoidance of alcohol and folate-containing vitamins during methotrexate treatment.
On day 1 of the single-dose protocol, obtain serum b-hCG, U&E, LFTs, FBC and blood group.
Advise women treated with methotrexate to wait at least 3 months before attempting conception.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A yolk sac, fetal pole or fetal cardiac activity significantly predicts treatment failure. A smaller pretreatment rise in serum b-hCG favours success; a rise of up to 11–20% over 48 hours was associated with higher success in cited studies. Haemodynamic instability, intrauterine pregnancy, breastfeeding, inability to comply with follow-up, known sensitivity to methotrexate, chronic liver disease, pre-existing blood dyscrasia, active pulmonary disease, immunodeficiency and peptic ulcer disease are listed contraindications.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Clinically stable women with an ectopic pregnancy diagnosed on ultrasound, minimal pain, willingness and ability to attend follow-up, and an initially decreasing serum b-hCG less than 1500 iu/l.
decision_rules: Expectant management is an option when the initial serum b-hCG is less than 1500 iu/l and falling.
Continue clinical and biochemical surveillance while the woman remains suitable; reassess treatment if pain develops or serum b-hCG rises persistently.

recommended_regimens.name: expectant management
recommended_regimens.summary: Observe selected, counselled and clinically stable women instead of intervening immediately.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reported success rates range from 57–100%, depending strongly on selection. In one prospective observational study, 146/333 ectopic pregnancies were managed expectantly, with success in 71.2% (104/146). A separate study reported 96% success when serum b-hCG was less than 175 iu/l and 66% when it was 175–1500 iu/l.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Follow until serum b-hCG is less than 20 iu/l in the cited prospective observational protocol; its repeat-test intervals varied between 2 and 7 days.

response_assessment.timepoint: During follow-up; between 2 and 7 days between repeat tests in the cited observational protocol
response_assessment.method: Serum b-hCG and assessment of symptoms
response_assessment.interpretation: In that protocol, expectant management stopped if the woman opted out, developed significant pain, had a sustained serum b-hCG increase or reached greater than 2000 iu/l.

supportive_care: Counsel the woman and ensure that she can attend follow-up.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited observational protocol also required no abdominal pain, no significant haemoperitoneum, a mass less than 30 mm in mean diameter, no embryonic cardiac activity and consent. In a cited multicentre RCT that largely included PULs, primary treatment success was 31/41 (76%) with single-dose methotrexate and 19/32 (59%) with expectant management; the investigators found no difference in primary success, but only 15 (15/73; 21%) pregnancies were visualised ectopic pregnancies.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with persistent trophoblast after salpingotomy.
decision_rules: Use serial serum b-hCG after salpingotomy to identify levels that fail to decline as expected.
Consider methotrexate if serum b-hCG plateaus or begins rising; counsel that salpingectomy may also become necessary.

recommended_regimens.name: methotrexate
recommended_regimens.summary: The guideline describes administration when persistent trophoblast is indicated by plateauing or rising serum b-hCG after salpingotomy.

alternative_regimens.name: salpingectomy
alternative_regimens.summary: Further surgery may be required after salpingotomy.

response_assessment.timepoint: 7 days after salpingotomy, then weekly until negative
response_assessment.interpretation: NICE recommends this surveillance schedule; failure to fall as expected suggests persistent trophoblast.

supportive_care: Before salpingotomy, counsel about the risk of persistent trophoblast and possible additional treatment.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Methotrexate at 50 mg/m2 has been widely used instead of repeat surgery, but the guideline states that formal comparative studies have not been performed.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with cervical pregnancy for whom conservative treatment is appropriate.
decision_rules: Methotrexate may be considered.
Earlier diagnosis, gestational age less than 12+0 weeks, absence of fetal cardiac activity and lower serum b-hCG are associated with more successful conservative treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: methotrexate
recommended_regimens.summary: Medical management may be considered for cervical pregnancy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A retrospective review of 62 cases estimated systemic methotrexate efficacy at approximately 91%, although protocols differed and successful cases also required surgical debulking or local methotrexate injection. In that review, gestational age more than 9+0 weeks, b-hCG greater than 10 000 iu/l, crown–rump length greater than 10 mm and fetal cardiac activity were associated with a higher risk of primary failure.

alternative_regimens.name: local injection with potassium chloride or methotrexate
alternative_regimens.summary: These local injection approaches are described among treatments for cervical pregnancy; combination with intra-amniotic injection appeared to increase success in a cited retrospective study.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A serum b-hCG greater than 10 000 iu/l is associated with a lower chance of successful methotrexate treatment. Uterine artery ligation and uterine artery embolisation (UAE) have been described as adjuncts to control haemorrhage, but reports are small and complications have been reported.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with life-threatening bleeding from cervical pregnancy.
decision_rules: Reserve surgical management for life-threatening bleeding because surgical methods have a high failure rate.

alternative_regimens.name: dilatation and curettage
alternative_regimens.summary: This historically used operation may be accompanied by haemorrhage-control measures.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Restrict its use to women for whom other measures are unsuitable; excessive bleeding requiring hysterectomy has been frequent.

not_recommended.name: routine surgical management
not_recommended.reason: Surgical methods have a high failure rate and should be reserved for life-threatening bleeding.

supportive_care: Uterine artery ligation or uterine artery embolisation (UAE) has been described to control haemorrhage.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Small reports of haemorrhage-control methods combined with intracervical or systemic methotrexate describe infection, uterine infarction, sciatic nerve injury and bladder or rectal necrosis.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with first trimester caesarean scar pregnancy.
decision_rules: Consider medical or surgical intervention, with or without additional measures to control bleeding.
Evidence is insufficient to recommend one particular intervention over another, although the guideline reports that the available literature favours surgery over medical treatment for effectiveness.
Counsel women about the associated severe maternal morbidity and mortality.

recommended_regimens.name: surgical treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: The literature described in the guideline supports a surgical approach as more effective, without establishing one specific intervention as preferred.

alternative_regimens.name: methotrexate
alternative_regimens.summary: Medical treatment may be given by ultrasound-guided injection into the gestational sac or by systemic intramuscular injection; local injection appears more effective for ending the pregnancy.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: An intervention considered for first trimester caesarean scar pregnancy, potentially with additional haemostatic measures.

alternative_regimens.name: suction evacuation
alternative_regimens.summary: Evacuation is a described surgical option; cervical cerclage, Foley catheter insertion or UAE has been combined with it for haemostasis.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selection depends on the clinical circumstances; the guideline does not establish one preferred procedure.

alternative_regimens.name: hysteroscopic resection
alternative_regimens.summary: Resection by hysteroscopy is a described surgical method.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selection depends on the clinical circumstances.

alternative_regimens.name: open, laparoscopic or transvaginal excision
alternative_regimens.summary: Excision can include scar repair, but is technically more demanding and invasive.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selection depends on the clinical circumstances.

supportive_care: Consider additional haemostatic measures alongside intervention when appropriate.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: With medical treatment, trophoblast remains in place and may bleed as vascular tissue degenerates; some authors have advocated adding suction evacuation. Whether scar repair reduces later recurrent scar pregnancy or scar rupture is unknown. Clinically stable women should be managed by a multidisciplinary team with relevant expertise.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with a small, nonviable scar pregnancy; or women whose pregnancy is partly implanted in the scar, grows into the uterine cavity and who decline termination after counselling.
decision_rules: Expectant management may be suitable for a small, nonviable scar pregnancy.
It may also be considered for a pregnancy partly implanted in the scar and extending into the uterine cavity if the woman declines termination after discussion of the risks.

alternative_regimens.name: expectant management
alternative_regimens.summary: Observation may be considered only in the circumstances described by the guideline.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: A small nonviable pregnancy, or a partly scar-implanted pregnancy growing into the uterine cavity when the woman declines termination after counselling.

supportive_care: Counsel about haemorrhage and morbidly adherent placentation.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline describes an uncertain natural history and serious maternal risks. Among 35 reported continuing pregnancies diagnosed in the first trimester, there were 27 live births and 22 emergency hysterectomies at gestational ages from 15 to 38 weeks.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with an ongoing second trimester caesarean scar pregnancy.
decision_rules: Balance the risk of intervention against the risk of continuing pregnancy in an attempt to reach a potentially viable gestational age.
Establish a care plan for morbidly adherent placenta and emergency intervention if haemorrhage or rupture occurs.
supportive_care: Arrange care for morbidly adherent placenta and plan emergency treatment for haemorrhage or rupture.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline describes a high risk of maternal morbidity and hysterectomy regardless of the approach taken.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Clinically stable women with low or significantly falling serum b-hCG.
decision_rules: Nonsurgical care is acceptable in a stable woman.
Restrict expectant management to women with low or substantially falling serum b-hCG for whom adding methotrexate may not improve the outcome.

recommended_regimens.name: expectant management
recommended_regimens.summary: Observation is suitable only under the specified clinical and biochemical conditions.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A case series of 19 women managed expectantly reported an 89.5% success rate.

response_assessment.interpretation: The initial value and whether levels fall substantially inform the likelihood of conservative success.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: In a case series of 42 women receiving expectant or medical management, initial b-hCG was lower among those with successful outcomes than among those without success (3216 iu/l versus 15 900 iu/l; P < 0.05).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Clinically stable women for whom pharmacological nonsurgical management is appropriate.
decision_rules: Methotrexate is an effective pharmacological option.
Evidence is insufficient to favour local over systemic administration.

recommended_regimens.name: methotrexate
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat medically when appropriate; the guideline does not recommend one route over the other.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: One observational study of 17 women treated with systemic methotrexate 50 mg/m2 reported no complications; another study reported adverse effects in 40% of women receiving systemic methotrexate. An Australian series of 13 pregnancies reported 91% success with single-dose intravenous methotrexate and oral folinic acid rescue.

alternative_regimens.name: transvaginal ultrasoundguided aspiration and intrasaccular methotrexate
alternative_regimens.summary: The described technique aspirates exocoelomic fluid and injects 25 mg of methotrexate, with/without 0.2–0.4 mEq of potassium chloride; reported success was 91%. It is technically more challenging.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: A described local-treatment approach when an appropriately trained clinician can perform the procedure.

not_recommended.name: other nonsurgical methods
not_recommended.reason: Evidence on safety and complications in future pregnancies is insufficient to recommend them.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The overall management decision also depends on symptoms, pregnancy size, fetal cardiac activity and serum b-hCG. Selective UAE with methotrexate has been reported, but future-pregnancy safety and complications are uncertain.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women selected for surgical treatment of interstitial pregnancy.
decision_rules: Laparoscopic cornual resection or salpingotomy is an effective surgical option.
Hysteroscopic resection under laparoscopic or ultrasound guidance could be an alternative.

recommended_regimens.name: laparoscopic cornual resection or salpingotomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Either laparoscopic operation is described as effective surgical management.

alternative_regimens.name: hysteroscopic resection
alternative_regimens.summary: Resection under laparoscopic or ultrasound guidance could be considered.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline also reports other endoscopic and haemostatic techniques, without establishing them as preferred approaches.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with cornual pregnancy involving a rudimentary horn.
decision_rules: Excise the rudimentary horn by laparoscopy or laparotomy to avoid recurrence.

recommended_regimens.name: excision of the rudimentary horn
recommended_regimens.summary: Remove the rudimentary horn laparoscopically or by laparotomy.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: When using laparoscopy, consider possible urinary tract anomalies associated with unicornuate uteri. Methotrexate and potassium chloride injection before later horn excision has been reported, but the guideline favours excision to prevent recurrence.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women whose ovarian ectopic pregnancy is diagnosed or requires confirmation at laparoscopy.
decision_rules: If laparoscopy is needed for diagnosis, favour definitive surgical treatment at that time.
Prefer removal of gestational tissue by enucleation, or wedge resection for a large ectopic mass.

recommended_regimens.name: laparoscopic surgical treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Minimally invasive surgery is the preferred treatment; blunt enucleation limits damage to adjacent ovarian tissue, while wedge resection is an option for a large mass.

alternative_regimens.name: oophorectomy
alternative_regimens.summary: Removal of the ovary is occasionally required.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Coexisting ipsilateral ovarian pathology or excessive bleeding.

supportive_care: Electrocautery or suturing may be used for haemostasis.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline advises that future fertility prospects after laparoscopic management are good.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with ovarian ectopic pregnancy for whom surgery carries a high risk.
decision_rules: Systemic methotrexate can be used when the risk of surgery is high.

alternative_regimens.name: systemic methotrexate
alternative_regimens.summary: Medical treatment is an option when surgery presents a high risk; successful and unsuccessful cases have both been reported.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: One series reported a 40% failure rate with methotrexate alone, and all successfully treated cases in that series had been diagnosed laparoscopically. The guideline states that selection criteria and treatment and follow-up regimens have not been defined.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with persistent residual trophoblast or persistently raised serum b-hCG after surgery for ovarian ectopic pregnancy.
decision_rules: Systemic methotrexate can be used postoperatively when residual trophoblast persists or serum b-hCG remains elevated.

alternative_regimens.name: systemic methotrexate
alternative_regimens.summary: The guideline permits postoperative medical treatment for persistent trophoblast or b-hCG elevation.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Persistent residual trophoblast or persistently raised serum b-hCG after surgery.

response_assessment.method: Serum b-hCG and assessment for residual trophoblast
response_assessment.interpretation: Persistent elevation or residual trophoblast may lead to consideration of systemic methotrexate.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline does not define a methotrexate treatment or follow-up regimen specifically for ovarian ectopic pregnancy.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with early abdominal pregnancy, particularly when the implantation site is not vascular.
decision_rules: Laparoscopic removal is an option for early abdominal pregnancy.
The guideline identifies early diagnosis and an implantation site away from a vascular area as circumstances in which laparoscopic treatment is safe and effective.

recommended_regimens.name: laparoscopic removal
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider laparoscopic removal for early abdominal pregnancy.

alternative_regimens.name: systemic methotrexate with ultrasoundguided fetocide
alternative_regimens.summary: The guideline describes this as a possible alternative treatment.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Early abdominal pregnancy when an alternative to removal is being considered.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Very few nonsurgical cases have been reported. Methotrexate has also been described as an adjunct to surgery.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with advanced abdominal pregnancy.
decision_rules: Undertake laparotomy promptly after diagnosis.
Plan the incision to avoid the placenta.
If placental vascular attachment involves major vessels or vital structures, it may be left in place to undergo spontaneous resorption.

recommended_regimens.name: laparotomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Use an open surgical approach for advanced abdominal pregnancy.

supportive_care: Use ultrasound and/or MRI to map placental location before laparotomy.
When indicated by placental location, plan the surgical team, blood products, preoperative angiographic embolisation, bowel preparation or ureteral catheters.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Leaving the placenta in situ is associated with ileus, bowel obstruction, fistula formation, haemorrhage and peritonitis, although the guideline reports lower mortality than with placental removal. Adjuvant methotrexate and selective arterial embolisation have been described.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Clinically stable women with a coexisting intrauterine pregnancy.
decision_rules: Include the prognosis of the intrauterine pregnancy and the woman's wishes in treatment decisions.
Local injection with aspiration is an option in clinically stable women.
Surgical removal is also an option in stable women.

alternative_regimens.name: local injection of potassium chloride or hyperosmolar glucose with aspiration of the sac contents
alternative_regimens.summary: Treat the extrauterine pregnancy locally while taking account of risks to the coexisting intrauterine pregnancy.

alternative_regimens.name: surgical removal
alternative_regimens.summary: Removal of an accessible ectopic pregnancy is an option even when the woman is haemodynamically stable.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Clinical stability and a surgically accessible ectopic pregnancy, such as a tubal, cervical or interstitial heterotopic pregnancy.

not_recommended.name: methotrexate when the intrauterine pregnancy is viable and the woman wishes to continue it
not_recommended.reason: The guideline states that methotrexate is not an option in this circumstance and that even local injection affects the intrauterine pregnancy.

response_assessment.interpretation: Confirm resolution of the ectopic pregnancy; b-hCG cannot be used for this purpose.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: For local treatment, the guideline describes hyperosmolar glucose injection into the extrauterine sac or potassium chloride injection into the fetal pole if possible, otherwise into the sac, together with aspiration. During laparoscopy, avoid uterine cannulation or manipulation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Haemodynamically unstable women with heterotopic pregnancy.
decision_rules: Choose surgical removal of the ectopic pregnancy when the woman is haemodynamically unstable.
Take the coexisting intrauterine pregnancy into account when planning treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: surgical removal
recommended_regimens.summary: Surgery is the method of choice in haemodynamic instability.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: If laparoscopy is undertaken, avoid cannulation or manipulation of the uterus.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women whose heterotopic ectopic pregnancy appears nonviable on ultrasound.
decision_rules: Expectant management is an option when ultrasound indicates that the ectopic pregnancy is nonviable.

alternative_regimens.name: expectant management
alternative_regimens.summary: Observation may be chosen for a heterotopic pregnancy with ultrasound evidence of nonviability.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Ultrasound findings indicate a nonviable ectopic pregnancy.

response_assessment.interpretation: Assess the ectopic pregnancy because serum b-hCG cannot establish its resolution in heterotopic pregnancy.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline cites expectant management of an interstitial heterotopic pregnancy in a symptom-free woman whose ultrasound showed that the interstitial pregnancy was not ongoing.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women whose intrauterine pregnancy is nonviable or who do not wish to continue the pregnancy.
decision_rules: Consider methotrexate only if the intrauterine pregnancy is nonviable or the woman does not wish to continue it.
Use particular caution because even local methotrexate injection affects the intrauterine pregnancy.

alternative_regimens.name: methotrexate
